newsitem.title: USA: NYC says retail buyers order $206 mln of its bonds.
newsitem.headline: NYC says retail buyers order $206 mln of its bonds.

text.p: Retail buyers ordered another $73 million of New York City bonds in a presale period but the $206 million total, while average, was about one third short of a near-record set in April, a city official said Tuesday.

Seeking high yields, retail investors bought out the three longest maturities in the approximately $740 million refunding that hits the market on Wednesday, enabling the city to close those issues out, along with the 2011 maturity.
New York City found it economical to buy bond insurance for about $250 million of the new bonds, said the city official, who declined to be named.

Individual investors were attracted to the higher yields offered by the the longer bonds, he added, noting they carried six-percent coupons. The six-percent level often is seen as a minimum level needed to draw small buyers.
"I would say this is a healthy, average order period. The interesting benefit is that we were able to sell out the longer-end," the city official said.
